title: Pow(x, n)
keyIdea: Write n in binary. Square x over and over (x, x², x⁴, x⁸…) and multiply the answer by the powers whose bit is 1: x¹³ = x⁸ · x⁴ · x¹. That is about log₂ n steps. For negative n use 1/x, and keep n in a long long because −(−2³¹) overflows an int.

approaches.name: Binary exponentiation
approaches.idea: I wrote this one (you didn't paste code). N = |n| as long long, x = 1/x if n < 0; while N > 0: if the lowest bit is 1, ans *= x; x *= x; N >>= 1.
approaches.why: One loop step per bit of n; three variables.
